subject: How to consider an auxiliary (integer) parameter (not to be differentiated wrt)

messages.author: 21316508443f4524
messages.subject: How to consider an auxiliary (integer) parameter (not to be differentiated wrt)
parts:
Dear all,
I'm trying to use TMB in a stochastic gradient framework. In the simple context of linear regression my idea is the following :
- Pass the whole Y vector and X design matrix as DATA
- Pass as PARAMETER both the beta coefficients vector (Y = X %*% beta ) and an auxiliary variable i, casted from Type to double to int; this auxiliary variable then is used to choose the observation used to compute the gradient of the objective function.

here is the code adapted from the basic linear regression example :

#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  DATA_VECTOR(Y);
  DATA_VECTOR(x);
  PARAMETER(a);
  PARAMETER(b);
  PARAMETER(i);
  
  //PARAMETER(logSigma);
  double j_double = asDouble(i);
  int j = int(j_double);
  //Type nll = -sum(dnorm(Y, a+b*x, exp(logSigma), true));
  Type diff = Y(j)-(a + b*x(j)) ;
  Type nll = pow( diff , Type(2.0) );
  
  REPORT( i );
  REPORT( j_double );
  REPORT( j );
  REPORT( Y(j) );
  REPORT( x(j) );
  REPORT( a + b*x(j) ) ; 
  REPORT( Y );
  REPORT( x );
  REPORT( nll );
  REPORT( diff );
  
  return nll;
}

Here is th R code calling TMB :

set.seed(123)
n = 100
p_data <- list(Y = rnorm(100) + 1:100, x = 1:100)
parameters <- list(a=10, b=-50, i = 1)

compile("test_index_as_param.cpp") # The C++ code above
dyn.load(dynlib("test_index_as_param"))

obj <- MakeADFun(p_data, parameters, DLL="test_index_as_param")




The various report are here to check if everything is working correctly but it isn't.
I call obj the result of MakeADFun
I can get the value of the objective function for a value of the parameters v_par from a call obj$fn(v_par) or obj$report(v_par)$nll

  • For v_par = c(0,0,1) I get  obj$fn(v_par) = 3.132272 and obj$report(v_par)$nll = 3.132272 -> GOOD !
  • For v_par = c(0,0,2) I get  obj$fn(v_par) = 3.132272 and obj$report(v_par)$nll = 20.78182 -> BAD !
  • For v_par = c(0,1,1) I get  obj$fn(v_par) = 0.05298168 and obj$report(v_par)$nll = 0.05298168 -> GOOD ! 
  • For v_par = c(0,1,2) I get  obj$fn(v_par) = 0.05298168 and obj$report(v_par)$nll = 2.429572 -> GOOD !
Actually I realize that the calculation of the function and the gradient does not react to a variation of the 3rd variable, it is fixed to its initial value, the one chosen when MakeADFun is called. But the expected calculations are performed as is shown by the reported values. 

Is it caused by the brutal cast Type -> double -> int ?
Where am I wrong ?
Does anyone have an idea to circumvent that issue ?
More generally, is it possible to define an objective function with 2 kind of parameters : the ones to calculate the derivatives and others that are auxiliary parameters (a bit like DATA but which can change at every call of the gradient function) ?
In any case, did anyone already use TMB for stochastic gradient like computations ?

Thanks a lot.

parts:
You can code up a stochastic gradient using the DATA_UPDATE feature. Here's an example:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_syntax/data_update.R
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_syntax/data_update.cpp

And here's the documentation:

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/group__macros.html

Note that the auxiliary index won't be needed. You do the accumulation of function value and gradient on the R side by changing obj$env$data and re-evaluating obj$fn and obj$gr.

Your simple linear regression example should be changed to something like:

DATA_SCALAR(Y); DATA_UPDATE(Y);
DATA_SCALAR(x); DATA_UPDATE(x);
PARAMETER(a);
PARAMETER(b);
Type diff = Y - (a + b*x) ;
